answers.rationale: Monday-morning arrival is proportionate because the first obligation is Monday afternoon and the local lead already has the room and kit. The prior-night and prior-day options add buffer without a stated setup dependency. The lifeline shows context-sensitive use of same-day arrivals when timing is adequate and prior-night positioning when a hard check-in leaves no slack, not a fixed arrival-day preference.

The first firm block is after lunch and the host is staging the tablets, so a Tuesday-morning arrival is the calibrated lower-friction choice. Monday evening is extra protection but is not operationally required by the stated facts; Sunday arrival is excessive. Prior travel decisions vary with setup timing and required check-in windows rather than reflecting a stable preference for arriving the night before.

A Wednesday-morning arrival fits a Wednesday-afternoon rehearsal when the local team already has the test cart. Tuesday evening provides more buffer than the scenario establishes as necessary, while Monday evening and Tuesday-morning work positioning are overbuilt. The history supports schedule-specific risk decisions, not a fixed rule to arrive a day early.

With a downtown convention-center forum, normal meeting luggage, and only one Midtown dinner, rideshare from DTW plus walking and local rideshares is the proportionate choice. A full-trip SUV or midsize rental adds parking and downtown-driving friction without solving an equipment or multi-site need; a one-day dinner rental is unnecessary. Prior no-car conference decisions were tied to urban, low-gear itineraries rather than a fixed transport preference.
